fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Capital T Truth Versus Facts", "body": "Chance opens by separating capital T truth from facts. In his view truth follows nature's template of wholeness, the fractal and the septenary repeating across scales, which is why he reads Plato's idea that all learning is remembering as learning about yourself. Facts, stories and history are human contrivances; he praises Juan's grip on the Jack Parsons story while calling it fact rather than truth. Juan answers with Nietzsche's perspectivism, arguing nobody interprets anything from an unbiased place and that dates and names deserve a grain of salt."}, {"title": "Why Chance Rejects Pop Culture Gnosticism", "body": "Asked by Juan about the dark Gnostic worldview, Chance draws a line between the Marty Leeds style of gnosis, where everything is God and you are its reflection, and the pop culture version of a prison planet run by an evil demiurge. He calls simulation theory the same Gnosticism repackaged in materialist form and says the only simulation we are in is the one inside our own head. When Juan asks who is really in charge, Chance offers what he calls his gnarliest conspiracy theory: nobody is."}, {"title": "Juan's Reptilian Overlords as Metaphor", "body": "Juan, raised Pentecostal, traces his signature phrase reptilian overlords to his deep dive into Gnosticism, and says he uses it in a metaphorical sense for forces at work in the world. He sketches Gnostic cosmology with Yaldabaoth as a Satan archetype ruling the lower aeons, and calls the sect that saw bodies as traps for angels a very dark view. His own leaning is emanationist: one source radiating out, with hardship, like hunting that keeps an ecosystem balanced, as the universe maintaining order. Chance recommends Pierre Sabak's books on dragon symbolism."}, {"title": "Chance on Archons as Self Made Filters", "body": "Chance argues that archons, the demiurge and egregores are real in a sense but hold no power over us. He describes layers of the body, physical, emotional and astral, and the nine chakras he works with, as filters between us and the undifferentiated pleroma. He says all boundaries are self imposed and frames archons as servitors we made and then forgot. Drawing on Abraxas from Jung's Seven Sermons to the Dead, he argues an adversary to existence cannot itself exist. Chance warns that his All Is Self axiom can tip into a god complex, and Juan adds it can excuse reckless living."}, {"title": "Religion, Free Will and Natural Law", "body": "Chance says he worships no specific deity but respects Jesus Christ symbolically, reading the name as meaning Jehovah is salvation and Jehovah as a verb for self existing life force, so following Christ means following nature's law. He links spirit with free will and argues there is a moral side to natural law. Juan recalls being told in church that works do not matter, calls the Bible a manual for being a good person, and counters that works matter because they shape how your life goes. Godfrey Higgins and Dylan Saccoccio frame Chance's case that scripture is allegory read as history."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Juan Ayala is the host of Juan On Juan, an insightful & hilarious podcast that takes deep dives into a variety of conspiratorial & occult topics. In this "swapcast" we interview each other, and create a fascinating conversation about discerning the Truth of nature & self, in opposition to the "facts" of narrative, history, and fiction. Are we facing archons, egregores, & a Demiurge (oh my!) or Archetypes, thought forms, and our imperial Self?
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: In the Plus+ Extension we get into secret societies, psychological warfare, the physics of love and fear, Watchers/Reptillians, Annunaki, simulation Theory, and so much more.
